topic_title: Top 10 Dog Breeds That Barely Shed
intro: If you're looking to keep your home a little cleaner and your allergies in check, choosing a low-shedding dog breed can make a big difference. These breeds tend to lose very little coat throughout the year, making grooming more manageable and minimizing fur around your living space. From elegant Poodles to charming Bichon Frises, this list highlights dogs known for their minimal shedding. Whether you're new to dog ownership or simply want a companion who doesn't leave a trail of hair wherever they go, these breeds are worth considering. Let's dive into the top low-shedding dogs that can bring joy without the extra cleanup.

picks.description: The Shih Tzu is a small, sturdy dog with a flowing double coat that doesn’t shed much but does require regular grooming to prevent mats. Their luxurious locks are often admired, but they’re also known for being a low-shedding breed, making them a popular choice for people wanting a pretty pup without the constant fur cleanup. Shih Tzus have a friendly, outgoing personality and thrive in family settings. Their affectionate nature means they love to be close to their humans, blending well into apartment living or homes with limited outdoor space.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers and families looking for a cuddly companion
picks.quirky_fact: Despite their regal appearance, Shih Tzus were bred to be lap dogs for Chinese royalty.

picks.description: Tiny but full of personality, the Yorkshire Terrier sports a fine, silky coat that sheds very little compared to other breeds. Yorkies are known for their feisty spirit and loyalty, making them great companions for those who enjoy a bold little dog. Their hair is more like human hair, which means it doesn’t shed like traditional dog fur but they do need regular brushing to keep their coat tangle-free. Their small size makes them perfect for city living, and they often bond strongly with their owners, providing plenty of affection and energy.
picks.best_for: City living and people looking for a spirited small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Yorkies were originally bred to catch rats in clothing mills.

picks.description: Miniature Schnauzers are spirited, intelligent dogs known for their distinctive beard and eyebrows. Their wiry double coat sheds very little, especially when regularly groomed and hand-stripped or clipped. This makes them a great option for those seeking a low-shedding breed with a lot of personality. They’re friendly and alert, often making excellent watchdogs without being overly aggressive. Their adaptable nature helps them fit well in homes of all sizes, and their moderate exercise needs keep them active but manageable companions.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting an alert and low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Miniature Schnauzers were bred to be ratters and farm dogs in Germany.

picks.description: The Bichon Frise is a small, cheerful dog with a fluffy white coat that sheds very little. Their curly fur traps shed hair, preventing it from scattering around your home. These dogs are known for their playful and affectionate nature, making them wonderful companions for people of all ages. They enjoy being part of family activities and usually get along well with other pets. Their grooming needs are moderate, requiring regular brushing and occasional trims to keep their curls looking their best, but the payoff is minimal shedding throughout the year.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a cheerful, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: Bichon Frises were once favored by French sailors for their cheerful temperament.

picks.description: Havanese dogs sport a soft, silky coat that sheds very little, making them a favorite among people seeking low-shedding breeds. These small dogs are known for their friendly and social nature, thriving on human interaction and often forming strong bonds with their families. Their expressive eyes and happy demeanor make them instantly lovable, and their adaptable size means they fit well in apartments or houses. Regular brushing helps keep their coat looking shiny and prevents mats, but they won’t leave much hair around your home.
picks.best_for: Social owners looking for a small, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: Havanese are Cuba's national dog and were prized by Cuban aristocracy.

picks.description: The Lagotto Romagnolo is a medium-sized breed known for its dense, curly coat that sheds very minimally. Originally bred as a water retriever and now famous for truffle hunting, this dog is intelligent and energetic. Their coat is unique — woolly and tightly curled — which helps trap shed hair and reduces dander. Regular grooming is essential to keep their curls healthy and free from mats. Lagottos are affectionate and devoted, making them excellent companions for active families who want a low-shedding dog with a bit of a working-dog edge.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting an intelligent, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Lagotto Romagnolos are often called "truffle dogs" because of their keen nose.

picks.description: Standard Poodles are renowned for their elegant appearance and distinctive curly coat that sheds very little. Their coat’s unique texture traps shed hair, which helps keep your home free from dog hair. Poodles are highly intelligent and trainable, known for their versatility in various activities from obedience to agility. They are also very social and thrive on mental stimulation and companionship. Regular grooming is necessary to maintain their coat, but the tradeoff is well worth it for those wanting a low-shedding, hypoallergenic breed that’s both stylish and smart.
picks.best_for: Families and individuals wanting a smart, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: Poodles were originally bred as water retrievers in Germany and France.

picks.description: Much like their Standard cousins, Miniature Poodles boast the same curly, low-shedding coat in a smaller package. They’re lively, intelligent, and easily trained, making them a popular choice for people seeking a compact dog that won’t fill their home with hair. Miniature Poodles love to be involved in family activities and adapt well to different living situations, including apartments. Their coat requires regular grooming and clipping, but they reward owners with minimal shedding and a lot of personality packed into a small frame.
picks.best_for: Compact living and active owners wanting a small, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Miniature Poodles excel at dog sports like obedience and agility.

picks.description: Toy Poodles are the tiniest members of the Poodle family but share the same signature curly coat that sheds very little. Their small size makes them a great fit for apartment dwellers or those wanting a lap dog with minimal shedding. Despite their delicate appearance, Toy Poodles are smart, alert, and eager to please, often surprising people with their agility and intelligence. As with other Poodles, regular grooming is necessary, but their low-shedding coat helps minimize fur in your living space.
picks.best_for: Apartment living and people wanting a small, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: Toy Poodles have been popular companion dogs for centuries.

picks.description: The Chinese Crested is truly unique with its mostly hairless body and tufts of hair on its head, feet, and tail. Because much of their skin is exposed, they shed almost nothing, making them one of the lowest-shedding breeds on the planet. Their unusual look turns heads, but they’re also known for being affectionate, lively, and playful. They require some skin care to keep their exposed areas healthy, but if low shedding is your top priority, the Chinese Crested is hard to beat.
picks.best_for: Owners seeking the lowest-shedding, unique companion
picks.quirky_fact: Chinese Cresteds come in two varieties: Hairless and Powderpuff (with a full coat).
